summary: metro-pop KV cache cold-start after geo-handoff causing elevated p95/p99 inference latency and streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovusRetail, dedicated) reports a sustained increase in inference tail latency and intermittent streaming timeouts beginning 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC. Impact appears correlated with a recent edge-pop routing handoff where requests originating in eu-west-1 are served from transient us-east-1 paths.

Impact:
- Increased p95/p99 generation latency for chat completions and streaming responses (p99 ~= 3.4s token stalls, increase from baseline ~600ms).
- Customer reports ~3% of streaming requests hitting client-side timeouts and aborted streams.
- Affects production customers behind a dedicated routing tag; revenue-impacting and triggers P1.

Environment:
- NovusRetail dedicated account, production.
- Primary traffic from eu-west-1 (EU) suddenly traversing to us-east-1 (US) after automatic pop handoff.
- Models: redwood-7b-quant (default), fallback gpt-4o-mini.

Observed behavior:
- Timeline shows region-affinity flip at 2026-03-12 09:15 UTC followed by gradual p50->p95 drift over ~30 minutes.
- Traces show extra TCP/TLS handshake and repeated KV cache misses for prefix caching (prefix-miss ratio jumped to 42%).
- Service logs show repeated 524-style streaming aborts from the edge-proxy after 9s.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use customer's account and send a batch of 1000 short-chat streaming requests (avg prompt 40 tokens) from eu-west-1.
2) Observe routing decision via /debug/route for account tag.
3) Inspect response timings and KV prefix hits on serving nodes.
4) Reproduce after forcing pop-handoff in the staging routing policy using canary rollouts (requires infra toggle).
observed_behavior: Routing handoff causes requests to land on remote serving nodes with cold KV cache; first-token generation frequently waits for KV fetch/warm path and extra TLS handshake across inter-region link. Median token latencies unaffected, but p95/p99 and streaming stalls increase noticeably.
expected_behavior: Requests should maintain POP-affinity; if handoff is required, KV pre-warm or parallel fetch should avoid adding >200ms additional per-request latency and avoid streaming timeouts.
logs_and_traces:
- Sample trace (tracing-id: 6b7f3a1e): edge-proxy handshake 120ms, cross-pop TLS 310ms, serving-runtime kv-miss wait 450ms, token-gen start.
- KV metrics: prefix_hit_rate dropped from 98% to 58% between 09:15-09:45 UTC.
- Edge proxy logs: 2026-03-12T09:22:11Z ERR stream aborted after 9.2s (client timeout).
- Link to Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/eu-west-pop-handoff?from=2026-03-12T09:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T10:00:00Z
investigation_notes:
- Oncall SRE (Daniel) confirmed routing change from the mesh: weight shift on geo-policy triggered handoff for subset of accounts (automation run ID infra-2026-03-12-005).
- Serving nodes in us-east-1 showed elevated kv_miss and cache-warmup traffic as expected.
- Network team reports transient BGP flap in the us-east transit that increased RTTs between pops by ~60ms during the same window.
- Hypothesis: combined effect of geo-handoff + inter-pop network jitter + cold KV cache causes compounded p99 latency and streaming aborts when client-side stream timeouts < additional latency.
- Repro on staging by flipping affinity produced similar p95 increase but smaller p99 due to lower inter-pop RTTs.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Logged by customer at 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC after multiple customer reports; escalated to SRE oncall.
Daniel Huang (SRE): Confirmed pop weight change and observed kv cold-start. Turning down the canary routing weight for NovusRetail to restore affinity as immediate mitigation.
Network (L3): Observed transient route churn between our eu transit and us-east; not yet correlated to infra automation. Raised ticket with transit provider. (see #network-incident-224)
CS Contact (Emma Li): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (restore affinity) and requested postmortem and action on preventing warmup regressions during handoffs.
workarounds:
- Immediate: Roll back routing weight to restore eu-west-1 affinity for NovusRetail (done 2026-03-12 10:40 UTC).
- Short-term: Increase client streaming timeout to 15s for affected customers via per-account config; inform CS to advise customers.
- Operational: Add pre-warm/task to fetch KV prefixes in parallel when routing handoff is detected (see next steps).
root_cause: A geo-affinity handoff triggered serving requests to remote nodes without performing KV prefix pre-warm. Concurrent transient network RTT increase amplified extra handshake and KV fetch latency, pushing many streaming requests past client timeouts.
resolution:
- Rolled back routing weight to original POP affinity which restored prefix hit rate and reduced p99 back to baseline by 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC.
- Added short-term per-account increased streaming timeout for NovusRetail.
- Created infra PR to add parallel KV prefetch for cross-pop handoff and to gate canary rollout with a KV warmup check (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8791).
next_steps:
1) Merge and deploy infra PR for KV pre-warm (owner: infra-team, ETA 2026-03-18).
2) Add routing-policy guard rails to block automatic affinity flips for dedicated accounts until warmup passes.
3) Postmortem to be published in Confluence and shared with NovusRetail.
4) Run chaos test that simulates POP handoffs and measures warmup penalties (SRE / Reliability).
